title: Fish Audio raises $50M seed to build AI voice models for creators and enterprises
summary: Fish Audio raised a $50 million seed round to expand its AI voice model platform, which has grown to 8 million users and generates $21 million in annual recurring revenue. The funding validates strong market demand for customizable voice synthesis among creators and enterprises.
content: Since launching last year, the startup today has more than 8 million people using the open-source or hosted version of its models, and now generates annual recurring revenue of $21 million.

content:

title: You don’t need to splurge on an expensive handheld fan to beat the heat
summary: Affordable JisuLife handheld fans priced at $25-33 offer a practical alternative to premium options like Dyson's $99-150 models, with comparable battery life and functionality. Budget-conscious consumers can achieve effective personal cooling without premium brand pricing.
content:
It’s not fancy, but it gets the job done for hours and hours on a single charge.	

Despite what influencers may say, you don’t need to spend $99.99 on Dyson’s HushJet Mini Cool or $149.99 for the Shark ChillPill to survive the summer whenever you leave the comfort of air-conditioning. My family has found all the comfort it needs to survive humid baseball games, sweltering concerts, and sweaty hikes with a couple of affordable handheld fans from a Chinese company called JisuLife that has spent the past decade honing its hardware.
At the start of the summer, I impulse-purchased a pair of JisuLife Life10 S fans from Costco, which at CDN $25 each (or $32.99 through Amazon), are among the most basic offerings from the company. JisuLife’s extensive lineup includes some fan models costing close to $100 with features like reverse-charging to power your phone and 100 different speed settings. I want all those features, but my goal was to not spend several hundred dollars on personal cooling devices that could easily go missing or get damaged during the chaos of summer activities.
The Life10 S’ functionality is comparatively basic, but also easy to use. A sliding power switch on the back prevents it from accidentally turning on while banging around inside a backpack, and a single button on the front cycles through five different fan speeds. There’s also a basic LCD display showing the battery’s remaining charge when the fan is first powered on and the current speed setting. It’s simple, but the Life10 S does its one job quietly and for a surprisingly long time.
When Dyson announced its first handheld fan in April, I assumed the company that had developed an expertise in moving air had created a personal cooling device that would outperform everything else on the market. My spouse loves their Dyson hair dryer, and I was sure the HushJet Mini Cool would be my secret weapon for surviving hot and humid summers, even if at $99 it was a splurge. title: Logitech’s handheld plans are on ice — don’t expect a G Cloud 2 soon
summary: Logitech's new gaming division head indicated the company is not prioritizing a successor to its G Cloud handheld gaming device, focusing instead on other product categories. The decision marks Logitech stepping back from the competitive handheld gaming market.
content:
Logitech's new gaming boss, Robin Piispanen, tells me he likes the idea of gaming handhelds. "It's such a charming value proposition," he says, as we sip iced vanilla lattes at my local cafe. But he's not building one right now. He's not sure when or if Logitech should try again, after its underwhelming experiment with the Logitech G Cloud streaming handheld. 
"Right now, in this moment in time, there's bigger things for us to focus on than doing a second G Cloud," he tells me.

summary: Perplexity expanded its AI agent tool Personal Computer to Windows, enabling PCs to function as autonomous systems that can access local files and applications. The tool mirrors the Mac version launched in April and completes Perplexity's AI agent rollout across platforms.

The service mirrors car leasing models and arrives weeks after Apple raised device prices.
content:
This image shows which Apple devices are included in its new leasing program. | Image: Apple	

Apple has officially introduced "Apple Upgrade," a new leasing program that aims to make it easier to get your hands on the latest iPhone, Mac, iPad, and Apple Watch models. title: Smart rings are looking like my kind of AI gadget
summary: Smart rings are emerging as practical AI gadgets, leveraging significant advances in speech-to-text and dictation technology that rival or exceed premium standalone apps. The wearables offer a convenient form factor for hands-free AI assistance in daily workflows.
content:
Over the last few months, I've spent a lot of time talking to my computer. One underrated feature of the LLM revolution has been a remarkable leap in all kinds of dictation technology - even the fastest, cheapest models are getting very good at understanding and processing speech. I've tested lots of these apps, from WisprFlow to Monologue to Spokenly to Handy to so many others, and have found them all to be useful ways to quickly write emails, Slack messages, and more. title: Hugging Face is being used to easily undress women and children
summary: A security audit found that Hugging Face's open-source image editing models readily generate nonconsensual deepfakes with inadequate safety guardrails, unlike mainstream AI platforms. The repository's permissive approach to content moderation enables misuse without sufficient protective measures.
content:
Hugging Face isn’t doing much to prevent the AI models it hosts from spitting out sexualized deepfakes. | Image: Cath Virginia / The Verge | Photos from Getty Images	

Hugging Face is being used to make nonconsensual deepfakes, and the popular open-source AI model repository is doing very little to prevent it. That's according to a new report published by the European nonprofit AI Forensics, which found that seven out of the top nine image editing models hosted by Hugging Face readily complied with requests to undress women using simple prompts.
While most mainstream generative AI models like Google's Gemini and OpenAI's ChatGPT have guardrails in place to block prompts that undress or sexualize people, that seemingly isn't the case for the models on Hugging Face tested by AI Forensics. The nonprofit says …
